name: Docs Graph Result Ranking And Filtering
description:
The docs control plane can already traverse document graphs through axes such as `role`, `composition`, `trace`, `source`, and `evidence`. However, broad graph results can still be noisy: relevant documents are found, but the system does not consistently rank stronger results ahead of weaker ones, filter result views by role/kind/axis/actionability, or summarize large result sets for review and PRD authoring.

This PRD adds a rule-based graph result reranking layer on top of existing graph traversal. It follows the standard retrieval/rescore pattern: traversal is the retrieval phase, and ranking/filtering is a post-traversal rescore/view phase. It must not change traversal semantics. It ranks, filters, and summarizes graph results after traversal so `docs graph`, `docs collect --graph`, and `docs prd context` can surface the most useful documents first while keeping the full raw traversal output available.

For backward compatibility, filters must not remove existing raw traversal fields such as `nodes`, `edges`, and `paths` from JSON output. Filtering and ranking are exposed through additive views such as `rankedNodes`, `filteredNodes`, `ranking`, or `summary`.

userStories.title: Define Graph Result Ranking Model
userStories.description: As a docs operator, I want a clear ranking model for graph results so that stronger document relationships appear before weak or broad matches.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a graph result ranking module that runs after traversal.
Ranking follows a retrieval/rescore pattern: traversal first, post-traversal reranking second.
Ranking does not modify traversal paths or edge discovery.
Rank factors include target node, path distance, axis, node kind, role, archive state, diagnostics, and follow-up category where available.
Same-family role docs rank above weak trace/context results.
Source/evidence-linked docs rank above broad context-only docs.
Archive/historical docs rank lower by default.
Ranking result includes `rank`, `score`, and `strength` or equivalent fields.
Ranking explanation includes factor-level reason metadata sufficient to debug score decisions.
Unit tests cover rank ordering for role, source, evidence, trace, context, and archive examples.

userStories.title: Add Graph Result Filters
userStories.description: As a docs operator, I want to filter graph result views so that I can inspect only the roles, kinds, axes, or follow-up categories relevant to a review.
acceptanceCriteria: Add filter parsing for relevant docs graph commands.
Support filtering by document kind, for example `--kind spec,todo,plan`.
Support filtering by role where role metadata exists, for example `--role spec,todo,plan`.
Support filtering by axis after traversal, for example `--filter-axis source,evidence`.
Document that `--axis` selects traversal axes, while `--filter-axis` filters the post-traversal result view.
Support active-view archive exclusion through ranked/filtered views without removing raw traversal nodes.
Support including archive documents explicitly, for example `--include-archive`.
Support filtering follow-up category where available, for example `--follow-up-category actionable,deferred`.
Filtering does not change traversal; it only changes additive returned/ranked/filtered views.
